_comment: Advisories that scripts/check_advisories.py has found in a tracked lockfile and that this
repository is KNOWINGLY carrying, each with the reason and the condition that retires it.
An advisory not listed here fails the build; an entry here whose advisory no longer appears
in any lockfile fails too -- a closed hold left recorded goes on excusing the finding, and
would silently re-cover it if the dependency rolled back. Same rule, both directions, as
docs/security-footguns.json and docs/script-test-coverage.json.
WHY A LEDGER RATHER THAN A SEVERITY FLOOR. The obvious way to make a new advisory scan green
is to gate it at `--severity high` and let the medium findings through unread. That buys a
passing check by not looking, and the two entries below are precisely the findings such a
floor would have hidden: 5.9 and 2.1. Naming them costs two JSON objects and keeps the set
of advisories this repository tolerates enumerated instead of implied by a threshold.
WHY BOTH ENTRIES ARE npm AND BOTH ARE BUILD-TIME. The first run of the scan over 1592 locked
packages in ten lockfiles found seven advisories. Five were FIXED in the same change rather
than recorded -- cryptography 49.0.0 -> 50.0.2 (CVSS 8.2), jupyter-server 2.20.0 -> 2.21.1
in three lockfiles (7.1), sharp 0.35.4 -> 0.35.5 (8.9) and source-map-js 1.2.1 -> 1.2.2
(8.7). So this file ships smaller than the gap it records, and the direction it is moving is
visible rather than asserted.
The cryptography fix is the one worth reading. .github/dependabot.yml held cryptography at a
semver-major ignore because mlflow 3.15.1's `requires_dist` said `cryptography<50,>=43.0.0`,
and its comment predicted the cost exactly: `cryptography is security-relevant and 49.x
carries no open advisory today, but that could change while the ceiling holds`.
PYSEC-2026-3552 is that change, and its fixed version is the 50.0.0 the ceiling forbade.
mlflow 3.16.1 has since raised the ceiling to `cryptography<51`, which is that hold's stated
LIFT THIS condition met -- so the advisory was fixable after all, and the only reason anyone
looked is that this scan started asking.
`exit` is required and is read by scripts/check_dependency_risk.py's fifth invariant, which
enforces the same `LIFT THIS` / `PERMANENT HOLD` discipline it already enforces for
dependabot.yml's `ignore:` entries, for the same reason: a hold justified by a temporary
fact becomes a permanent decision on the strength of that fact unless something re-asks the
question. `LIFT THIS` must name an upstream change someone can go and check.

holds.summary: Quadratic complexity in flat selector parsing allows CPU exhaustion (CVSS 5.9)
why: Capped two levels up, and by the CURRENT release of the capping package rather than a
stale pin of ours: @expressive-code/core 0.44.2 -- the latest, checked 2026-10-09 --
requires `postcss-nested ^6.0.1`, and postcss-nested 6.2.0 requires
`postcss-selector-parser ^6.1.1`. The fix is 7.1.6. Only postcss-nested 8.0.1 takes
`postcss-selector-parser ^7.1.4`, and nothing in the chain will accept postcss-nested 8
yet. @expressive-code/core arrives through @astrojs/starlight, which builds the
website's documentation code blocks.
The exposure is bounded by what the parser is fed. It runs at BUILD time over
expressive-code's own stylesheet during the website build, so the selectors are shipped
by the package itself, not supplied by anyone. CPU exhaustion against a static-site
build in CI is a slow build, and the website serves no CSS this parser touches at
request time. Recorded rather than dismissed because that reasoning is about where the
package sits today, and a future direct dependency on it would not be covered by it.
holds.exit: LIFT THIS when @expressive-code/core's `postcss-nested` range admits 8.x, or when any intermediate release pulls postcss-selector-parser >= 7.1.6. Re-check with `npm view @expressive-code/core dependencies`.

holds.summary: Existing prototype pollution can bypass trust restrictions (CVSS 2.1)
why: mermaid 12.1.0 -- the latest, checked 2026-10-09, one minor ahead of the 12.0.0 locked
here -- still requires `katex ^0.16.47`. The fix is 0.18.2, which that range cannot
reach, so bumping mermaid does not help and overriding katex to 0.18 would put mermaid
on a major it does not declare support for.
Same build-time bound as the entry above, with a narrower surface: katex renders maths
inside mermaid diagrams, and every mermaid diagram in this repository is authored in
docs/*.md by the people who commit it. The advisory needs attacker-controlled TeX to
reach the pollution, and there is no path by which untrusted input becomes a diagram
here. Lowest-severity finding of the seven, and the one a severity floor would most
obviously have swallowed, which is why it is written down instead.
holds.exit: LIFT THIS when mermaid's `katex` range admits 0.18 or later. Re-check with `npm view mermaid dependencies.katex`.
